title: The Broken Sigil
premise: Juniper Whitlock has spent his life copying prayers in the valley of Hollowmere, where the wards keep magic out and debtors like him in. When the wards shatter and the stars vanish, he learns his own blood is the missing half of an ancient covenant between the valley and the fae realm beyond. Hunted by both the temple that owns him and a fae envoy who claims kinship, Juniper must cross into a world he was raised to fear and reforge the broken sigil before winter swallows both realms. In the end, he pays the covenant's price himself—surrendering his name and memory to seal it—choosing belonging over survival, while those who loved him carry his story forward.
about_author: Freya Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval land charters before turning to fantasy. She writes about debt, borders, and the quiet people history forgets, from a farmhouse full of rescued cats.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Copying ledgers by candlelight, Juniper notices the stars vanishing one by one, then feels the valley wards snap like cut thread. The temple elders lock the gates and blame debtors. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine—the moment invisibility stops working.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Interrogated by High Warden Corvane, Juniper hides the sigil-shaped birthmark on his wrist. A stranger with silver eyes is dragged in from the border; their eyes meet and something recognizes something. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance as Juniper lies for the first time.

chapters.title: The Envoy in the Cell
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, night visit. The prisoner, Sylwen, reveals she is fae envoy and that Juniper's bloodline sealed the original covenant—and broke it. She offers escape. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity, learning his whole life was a cage built around him.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps
chapters.summary: Sylwen's POV. Escaping through flooded catacombs, Sylwen sees Hollowmere's true function: the wards don't keep magic out, they siphon it to feed the temple's masters. Emotional beat: cold clarity—she needs this soft-spoken scribe more than she admits.

chapters.title: Beyond the Wardline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They cross the border into a landscape where seasons have stopped mid-autumn. First fae ambush; Juniper's mark flares and turns a blade aside. Emotional beat: first taste of power and its cost—a piece of his warmth dies with each use.

chapters.title: The Court of Standing Frost
chapters.summary: Sylwen's POV. At the fae court, Juniper learns the truth: the temple lords stole the covenant's keystone to hoard magic, dooming both realms to endless winter. The court wants Juniper as a weapon, not a partner. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—he must choose between Sylwen's people and his own.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Captured by temple riders, Corvane offers freedom from debt if Juniper betrays Sylwen. Juniper pretends to accept, buying time, but the lie costs him Corvane's trust and Sylwen's when she overhears. Emotional beat: betrayal as strategy, loneliness as price.

chapters.title: The Keystone Below
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Reconciled by necessity, Juniper and Sylwen descend beneath the temple to the stolen keystone. Corvane, betrayed by his own masters, joins them at the last moment. Emotional beat: unlikely alliance forged in the dark; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Reforge the Sigil
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Climax: as winter falls for good, Juniper binds his blood, name, and memory into the keystone atop the temple spire while fae and mortals battle below. The stars reignite. Emotional beat: sacrifice as choice—he walks into the light knowing what he'll lose.

chapters.title: The Scribe Without a Name
chapters.summary: Sylwen's POV, epilogue tone. Spring returns; the valley opens its gates. A young scribe finds an old ledger in Juniper's hand and begins telling his story so the covenant remembers him. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—belonging achieved through story, not memory.
